Gordon, Bianca at Ocotillo wants a straight answer on whether the E119 companion simulation validated, for the launch materials. I can't close my review of the Phase 1 draft until section 7 exists, so I need the validation memo from you.

Work from the companion run as it stands, the appropriate test report and certification document, the amended numbers Bianca sent over, and the dimensioned assembly drawing. Our own procedure governs how the result gets reported. No new runs or tests are available and nothing is being asked of Red Butte or Ironwood, so this comes out of what is on the file server today, 10/10/2025, and nothing else on it needs changing.

Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on. I need the governing criterion and the time it is reached, and I need to know whether the prediction in the section 7 stub stands. I need the experimental value you adopt and your disposition on Bianca's figure. On the strength of those I need the error, the acceptance criterion, the uncertainty, and how the error compares against both. I also want the largest prediction that would have cleared the criterion.

Two comparisons belong in the memo as well: the minutes separating the two criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and how far the governing point sits above the nine point mean at governance in each. Tell me what they say about the model, where the rework belongs, and whether any of that rework has been started yet. I also need what all of this means for the rest of Phase 1.

The memo also needs what this exercise does and does not establish about Ocotillo's wildfire claim and what would close that gap, including the form any future comparison would have to be reported in. I need what Bianca's figure would do to the certified rating if it were ever substantiated and who is entitled to act on that, the stamp language, and my checklist disposition: which item the memo lets me close and which of the rest stay open. Give it to me as a Word memo with crossing times rather than the samples that trip them, times to the nearest minute, limits as they fall, and every number carrying its unit. Add a short paragraph I can send Bianca today.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

1. TEST STANDARD AND METHOD
The evaluation reported here was performed in accordance with ASTM E119, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests
of Building Construction and Materials (current edition). One vertical fire-endurance test was performed on the wall
assembly described in Section 2, using the standard time-temperature curve prescribed by ASTM E119. The

The assembly was tested as a non-load-bearing partition. The applicable fire-endurance criteria for a
non-load-bearing wall under ASTM E119 are the following two thermal-transmission conditions on the unexposed
face:
 Average unexposed-face criterion. The average temperature rise measured by nine thermocouples
symmetrically disposed on the unexposed face of the specimen shall not exceed 139 degC (250 degF) above the
initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.
 Single-point criterion. The temperature rise at any single thermocouple on the unexposed face shall not exceed
181 degC (325 degF) above the initial ambient temperature at any point in the test.
Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two thermal-transmission criteria governs the reported fire endurance for the
specimen.
2. SPECIMEN DESCRIPTION
One 3.05 m × 3.05 m (10 ft × 10 ft) specimen was constructed by the client at the Red Butte laboratory prior to test.
The specimen is a double-wythe 3D-printed concrete wall assembly consisting of two printed concrete leaves

Instrumentation on the unexposed face was applied by Red Butte technicians per ASTM E119. All thermocouples

3.1 Unexposed-face thermocouple layout
Nine thermocouples, designated TC-1 through TC-9, were installed on the unexposed face in the symmetric pattern

3.2 Position of TC-6 relative to tie course
The specimen was surveyed for tie positions before instrumentation was applied. During layout of the nine

The tie course crossing behind TC-6 constitutes a metallic path from the exposed leaf to the unexposed leaf at that

reported alongside the eight other unexposed-face thermocouples without adjustment or omission.
3.4 Furnace and ambient instrumentation
 Nine furnace thermocouples (TCF-1 through TCF-9) per E119, symmetrically placed within 6 in of the exposed

 Initial ambient (average of TC-A1, TC-A2 at t = 0): 21.0 degC.
3.5 Data acquisition
All thermocouple channels were logged at 1 Hz to a computerized data acquisition system with NIST-traceable

Per ASTM E119, the earlier of the two criteria governs the reported fire endurance. The single-point criterion was

The single-point governance at thermocouple 6 is consistent with the presence of the continuous steel tie course as a
metallic thermal-bridge path between the exposed and unexposed leaves at that location. The average
unexposed-face temperature rise across the remaining eight thermocouples did not approach the single-point

3. Certification
On the basis of the certified test identified in Section 1.1 and the governing endurance result stated in Section 2,
Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering certifies the assembly for a 1-hour fire-resistance rating (60 min).
The measured endurance of 118 min exceeds the 60-minute rung by a healthy margin. The next higher standard rung
is a 2-hour rating, which requires 120 min of demonstrated endurance under the governing criterion; the measured

higher rung.
Certification scope. This certification is limited to the specific assembly and test conditions described in Sections 1.2
and 1.3. It is not a statement about any other assembly, any other configuration of ties, cavity contents, leaf
thickness, or aggregate, or any other fire exposure than the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve.
4. Amendments and Reissuance
Any change to the certified rating requires a reissued test report from the testing laboratory of record and a new
certification issued by Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering. No other party may certify or restate this rating.
5. Limitations
5.1 Standard exposure only. The certified rating is a comparative assembly rating derived from performance under
the standard ASTM E119 time-temperature curve as delivered by a laboratory furnace. It is a measure of the
thermal-transmission behavior of the specific assembly described in Section 1.2 under a standard fire exposure.
5.2 Not a wildfire-performance statement. The ASTM E119 exposure is a standardized post-flashover

MEMORANDUM — PHASE 1 SCOPING

1.  Purpose & Scope
This memo fixes, at project kickoff and before any meshing is undertaken, the first-principles basis on which the Phase 1 wildfire-exposure large-eddy simulation set will be built. It records the design conditions taken from the site meteorological pull, the buffelgrass fuel model, the Rothermel-to-Byram source-term chain that produces the design fire, the Froude regime assessment inputs, and the LES sub-domain geometry against which downstream mesh sizing will be measured. It is issued on the effective date of the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work (CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01, signed 10/08/2025), before revC of the assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted with the SOW) is imported into the mesher.
The intent is that every downstream case-setup artifact, mesh-study artifact, and Phase 1 reporting deliverable — including the interim hand-calc due 10/13/2025 and the LES setup deliverable due 10/20/2025 — trace their source-term, regime, and geometry inputs back to the numbers recorded here, rather than re-argue them case-by-case. Where a downstream artifact needs the design fire heat release, the characteristic source diameter, or the plume length scale, it shall cite this memo.
The scope of Phase 1 as procured under Section 3.1 of the SOW is six transient wildfire cases (240 deg and 270 deg wind directions at 20-ft wind speeds of 5, 8, and 12 m/s). The fire source term and the sub-domain sizing recorded here apply to that entire matrix; they are not per-case parameters.
2.  Site Design Conditions
Design conditions are taken from the ten-year hourly record of the Pima County ALERT network for the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson (data pull: site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv, Section 3.1 of the SOW envelope). The following envelope governs Phase 1:

These conditions define the site for regime classification (Section 4 below) and for the source-term chain (Section 3 below). They are the same conditions carried into the Phase 1 report; no re-derivation is required.
3.  Fuel Model — Sonoran Buffelgrass at Site Design Conditions
The design fire source term is developed under the Rothermel spread-to-Byram intensity chain, evaluated at the site design conditions of Section 2. The buffelgrass fuel model is adopted per the SOW Section 2 definition (“Buffelgrass Fuel Model”). Fuel-model quantities are:
•  Fuel load (dry):  w = 0.6 kg/m²
•  Low heat of combustion:  h = 18,600 kJ/kg
•  Rate of spread at design wind:  R = 0.9 m/s
R is the head-fire rate of spread produced by the Rothermel surface-fire spread model for cured buffelgrass at the low-humidity, high-temperature, moderate-wind conditions of Section 2. It is used here as the input to the Byram fireline-intensity relation; the Rothermel-model input parameter tabulation for buffelgrass is on file with the project data pull.
Byram’s fireline intensity is the product of the low heat of combustion, the available fuel load per unit area, and the rate of spread:
I = h · w · R
  = (18,600 kJ/kg) × (0.6 kg/m²) × (0.9 m/s)
  = 10,040 kW/m
The Byram wind-tilted solid-flame length correlation gives:
L = 0.0775 · I^0.46
  = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
  = 5.4 m
L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:

The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
5.  LES Sub-Domain
The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
Q = I × L_segment
  = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
  = 30,120 kW
  = 30.1 MW
Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
•  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
•  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
   = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
   = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
D* = 3.76 m.
The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
6.  Wall Assembly Note
The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
7.  Downstream Inputs
The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
•  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
•  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
•  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
•  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
•  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
•  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
•  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
•  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.

Document: CFDME-QA-VAL-002 Author: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer (AZ PE

Principal Engineer (AZ PE #48213)
1. Purpose and Scope
This procedure governs how validation is performed, evaluated, and reported for every deliverable of The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC ("The CFD ME") that carries a validation claim. A validation claim is any statement,
quantitative or qualitative, that a simulation prediction reproduces a physical measurement within a stated tolerance.
Whenever such a claim is made — in a client report, a peer-review response, a testimony exhibit, or an internal
working record — the reasoning, arithmetic, and acceptance decision shall follow the steps set out here.
The scope covers all CFD analyses executed by staff engineers, remote engineers, and contracted vendors of the
firm, regardless of solver stack, regime, or client. It applies from the moment a validation reference is selected for a
project until the corresponding project file is closed and archived. Deviation from this procedure requires a written
waiver signed by both the reviewing engineer of record and the firm's owner, filed to the project's QA folder before the
deliverable is issued.
The procedure does not certify third-party test data, nor does it substitute for the engineering judgment of the
professional engineer of record. It fixes the form in which validation is expressed and the criterion against which it is
judged; it does not relieve any engineer of independent responsibility for the underlying analysis.
2. References
The following external standards inform this procedure. The firm holds single-user licenses to each; proprietary text is
not reproduced. The provisions relied upon are restated below in the firm's own words with citations back to the
source clause.
 ASME V&V 20-2009 (R2016), Standard for Verification and Validation in Computational Fluid Dynamics
and Heat Transfer. Framework for expressing validation as a comparison error with an associated validation
uncertainty. 
formulation restated in Section 3 below, 
 ASTM E119-24, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests of Building Construction and Materials. Referenced
for the exposure curve and the two thermal-transmission end-point criteria applied by testing laboratories. See
criteria whose interpretation is restated in Section 7.
 NIST NCSTAR 1-5 series, Fire Investigation of the World Trade Center Disaster, thermal-model validation
appendices. Cited for community practice on uncertainty accounting in conjugate fire-thermal problems; not
binding.

3. Model-Error Formulation
Validation shall be reported as the model error E = S - D with its validation uncertainty u_val, and never as a yes/no.
 S is the simulation prediction — the value produced by the CFD run using the model, mesh, solver, boundary
conditions, and material properties documented in the report.
 D is the certified experimental value — the corresponding measurement produced by the physical test of record,
drawn from the certified third-party report described in Section 6.
 E carries a sign. A positive E denotes a simulation that predicts more of the measured quantity than the test
observed; a negative E, less. The sign is retained through every downstream comparison and is required in every
rollup.
The equation E = S - D is the reporting form. Every deliverable that carries a validation claim shall present S, D, E,
and u_val in a single line or table, in that order, with a citation to the physical test report from which D is taken and to
See ASME V&V 20 Section 1 (validation framework and definitions) for the source
and Section 5 for the components combined in Section 4 below.
ASTM E119 Section 8 (thermal transmission on the unexposed face · average rise and single-point) for the
Internal: CFD Modeling Standards - Fire & Buoyant Flows(M. Falk, PE); QA Verification Standard -
Mesh & Resolution(M. Falk, PE); External Standards Digest(M. Falk, PE).
=== PAGE 2 ===
the run identifier from which S is taken. Descriptive words such as "matches," "agrees," "confirms," or "is validated"
are inadmissible substitutes for the numerical statement. The reviewing engineer shall reject any submitted
deliverable that omits any of the four quantities or that replaces the numerical rollup with a qualitative
characterization.
The requirement to report E with u_val — rather than a binary outcome — is not a matter of firm style. A yes/no
verdict conceals the sign and magnitude of the discrepancy, hides whether the disagreement is within measurement
scatter or resolved as a model error, and forecloses the diagnostic reasoning the validation exercise exists to support.
The reviewing engineer shall enforce the reporting form on every deliverable.
4. Uncertainty Build-Up
The validation uncertainty u_val is the root-sum-square (RSS) combination of three independent components, each
expressed in the units of the quantity being validated:
1. Numerical uncertainty, u_num. Reflects discretization, iterative convergence, and round-off contributions in S.
For the class of problem addressed in Section 8 — a conjugate thermal simulation of a compartment-wall assembly
under an ASTM E119 exposure — the firm's default value is ±4 min, established from prior three-grid conjugate
thermal studies on similar assemblies. A project-specific value shall be substituted where a resolution study or
convergence study supports one. 2. Input uncertainty, u_inp. Reflects propagation of uncertainties in material
properties (temperature-dependent conductivity, density, specific heat), boundary conditions (furnace-side
temperature histories, ambient side convective and radiative loss), and geometric idealization (leaf thickness, tie
diameter and spacing, cavity dimension). The firm's default value for the same class of problem is ±6 min. 3.
Experimental uncertainty, u_exp. Reflects instrument, calibration, and placement contributions to D as reported by
the testing laboratory. For calibrated Type-K thermocouples of the class used in ASTM E119 furnace work, the firm's
default value is ±5 min.
Combining by root-sum-square:
 u_val = sqrt( u_num^2 + u_inp^2 + u_exp^2 )
= sqrt( 4^2 + 6^2 + 5^2 )
= sqrt( 16 + 36 + 25 )
= sqrt( 77 )
= ±8.77 min
The result is reported to whole minutes: u_val = ±9 min for this class of problem.
Two guardrails apply.
First, the three components must be independent. If the numerical model uses lab-measured material properties
whose uncertainty is already folded into D, that property uncertainty shall not be double-counted in u_inp. The
reviewing engineer shall verify independence at the peer review stage.
Second, the default values shall be reviewed at least annually or whenever a project uses a materially different
assembly, exposure, or instrument class. A project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, u_exp shall be recorded in
the project QA folder before u_val is published.
5. Acceptance Criterion
The firm acceptance criterion is |E| ≤ 10% of D.
The criterion is scaled: it grows with the endurance value being validated, so short endurances demand tighter
agreement in absolute minutes and long endurances tolerate more. A 30-minute endurance carries a 3-minute band;
a 120-minute endurance carries a 12-minute band; a 240-minute endurance carries a 24-minute band. This scaling is
deliberate. Absolute-minute criteria are unstable across the range of assemblies the firm analyzes; a 5-minute
absolute tolerance is loose against a 30-minute rating and severe against a 4-hour rating. A percentage-of-D criterion
is stable across the range and disciplines short-endurance work where the absolute stakes are largest.
Two secondary tests accompany the primary criterion and shall appear in every validation rollup:
  Compare |E| to u_val. If |E| ≤ u_val, the discrepancy is within the combined validation uncertainty and is best
characterized as measurement-plus-model scatter. If |E| > u_val, the discrepancy is resolved as a model error —
larger than the noise floor of the exercise — and shall be treated as an actionable finding, regardless of whether

=== PAGE 3 ===
the primary 10% criterion is met.
 Compare the sign of E to the direction of the physical expectation. A simulation that consistently over-predicts
endurance carries different engineering implications from one that consistently under-predicts; the sign is
preserved in every rollup and discussed in the report narrative.
A deliverable in which |E| exceeds the criterion, or in which |E| exceeds u_val, or both, shall not be released with an
unqualified validation claim. The reviewing engineer determines whether the deliverable may be released with a
documented finding, whether the model shall be reworked, or whether the validation reference itself is unsuitable and
a different reference shall be sought.
6. Source of D
D shall be taken from the certified third-party test report of record. Client-amended values may not be
substituted for D absent a reissued report from the testing laboratory of record and a calibration certificate authorizing
the revision. Post-test amendments transmitted by the client but not authorized by the lab are not admissible as D.
The rule is strict for a reason. D is the physical anchor of the validation; if D moves for any reason other than a
documented laboratory action, the validation ceases to be against the physical test and becomes a comparison
against a preferred number. The two states are indistinguishable in the report if the substitution is silent, and the
record of the exercise is corrupted.
The following forms of documentation are required to substitute a revised D:
1. A reissued report from the testing laboratory of record, bearing the same report number as the original with an
amendment sequence (e.g., "-R1"), signed by the laboratory's authorized signatory, and stating the reason for the
revision. 2. A calibration certificate covering the instrument or measurement whose revision is at issue, with a date
and calibration-authority reference sufficient to trace the correction. 3. An explicit statement, in the reissued report,
that the revised value supersedes the value in the original report for all downstream use.
Absent any of the three, the original value stands. The reviewing engineer shall reject any deliverable that draws D
from a client-amended figure not backed by the above documentation. A polite, specific, thermocouple-calibration
explanation transmitted by a client is not a laboratory revision; the analyst shall record the client transmittal in the
correspondence folder and continue to use the certified D. Any pressure to depart from this rule — from schedule,
from commercial positioning, or from a persuasive account of what "really" happened at the test — shall be resolved
by returning to the reissued-report requirement.
7. Scope Limitation
ASTM E119 exposes an assembly to the standard building time-temperature curve, which is not a WUI
wildfire exposure. E119 endurance is therefore a comparative assembly rating, not a prediction of wildfire survival
time. Validation against E119 data validates the model against E119; it does not validate a wildfire performance
claim.
The distinction is not a formality. The E119 curve is a smooth, monotonically rising fuel-continuous compartment fire
scenario intended to grade the relative thermal performance of building assemblies under a repeatable exposure. A
wildland-urban interface exposure is a wind-driven, radiation-dominated, transient fire-front event whose peak heat
flux, duration, and spatial distribution differ from E119 at every axis. An assembly with a two-hour E119 rating is not
thereby a two-hour wildfire assembly, and no algebraic manipulation of an E119 result yields a wildfire survival time.
Firm practice on this point:
  Reports that use E119 test data to validate a CFD model shall state, in the validation section, that the validation
exercise establishes model fidelity against the E119 exposure and shall not extrapolate that finding to wildfire,
hydrocarbon-pool, or other non-E119 exposures.
 Where a project's ultimate objective is a wildfire performance claim, the validation section shall separately identify
(i) what E119 data validates, (ii) what it does not, and (iii) what additional physical evidence would be required to
close the gap.
 Marketing or commercial statements that translate an E119 rating into a wildfire performance figure are outside
the firm's stamp and shall not appear in any firm-issued deliverable.
8. Worked Example — Illustrative Assembly

=== PAGE 4 ===
The worked example below illustrates the arithmetic of Sections 3 through 5 using a hypothetical compartment-wall
assembly. The values used are illustrative and are not the values of record for any live project; they are pedagogic
only.
Inputs (illustrative).
 D = 120 min. Certified single-point endurance drawn from a hypothetical laboratory ASTM E119 report for the
illustrative assembly. The single-point criterion governs per ASTM E119.
 S = 126 min. Simulation prediction from a conjugate CFD run mirroring the E119 furnace exposure for the same
illustrative assembly.
 u_val = ±9 min. Per Section 4, using default values (u_num = ±4, u_inp = ±6, u_exp = ±5), combined by
root-sum-square.
Rollup (illustrative).
 E = S − D = 126 − 120 = +6 min. Reported as E = +6 min, sign retained.
 Primary criterion: 0.10 × D = 0.10 × 120 = 12 min. Comparison: |E| = 6 min ≤ 12 min. The primary criterion is
met.
 Secondary comparison to u_val: |E| = 6 min ≤ 9 min. The discrepancy is within the combined validation
uncertainty.
Conclusion (illustrative). |E| = 6 min ≤ 12 min criterion AND ≤ 9 min u_val. The illustrative simulation would validate
against the illustrative certified test under the primary criterion, with the discrepancy sitting within the combined
validation uncertainty.
The point of the worked example is the arithmetic and the reporting form, not the outcome. In practice the analyst
reads D from the certified third-party report per Section 6, computes S from the run of record, tabulates u_val per
Section 4, and applies Section 5 to arrive at an acceptance decision. The engineering action that follows from a
non-validating rollup — grid resolution review, boundary-condition audit, material-property review, geometric
idealization audit — is not a substitution of D. Section 6 governs D.
9. Stamp Boundary
The CFD analyst of record stamps CFD thermal analysis only. The firm's stamp block on any deliverable that carries
a validation claim under this procedure shall read:
Fire-resistance rating certification is reserved to the fire-protection professional engineer of record for the project.
Where the firm's CFD work supports a rating certification issued by a fire-protection PE, the firm's deliverable and the
fire-protection PE's certification remain separately stamped and separately scoped. A CFD validation finding under
this procedure is not a rating action; a rating action is not a CFD validation finding. Neither substitutes for the other,
and neither shall be represented as the other in any client-facing communication.
